checks.invariant: Every value interpolated unquoted into the sbatch script templates and the `bash -lc` strings of shinka/launch (env exports, `" ".join(cmd)`, log_dir, image/image_name, docker_flags, image_tar_path, modules, conda_env, activate_script, partition/time/cpus/gpus/mem, extra sbatch kwargs) originates from the operator's own job/evolution configuration and never from LLM output, a DB/results-dir value, a directory-walk config or a remote client.
checks.result: Holds; refuted as a finding. Origins traced: (1) eval_env for `export K=V` / `-e K=V` (slurm.py:20,27,481) comes only from JobScheduler._build_eval_env (scheduler.py:205-216): fixed keys with values '1'/'0', 'FALSE', 'PASSIVE' and str(max(1,int(n))) - no external string. (2) cmd (slurm.py:271,352,446,489) comes from JobScheduler._build_command (scheduler.py:152-203): 'python' or sys.executable/job.python_executable, job.eval_program_path, exec_fname_t, results_dir_t and job.extra_cmd_args. exec_fname_t/results_dir_t are built in async_runner.py:1594-1602 and 2605-2607 as f"{results_dir}/gen_{generation}/main.{lang_ext}" and ".../results": results_dir is evo_config.results_dir (operator), generation is an int, lang_ext is a fixed map lookup of evo_config.language. The LLM chooses no file name, patch name or path component that reaches cmd or log_dir (patch names are only stored/printed). (3) image, docker_flags, image_tar_path, modules, conda_env, activate_script, partition, time, cpus, gpus, mem are dataclass fields of the JobConfig passed to the runner (scheduler.py:241-270), populated from the operator's hydra config (launch_hydra.py:14, utils_hydra.py:73), from the operator-named --config file / --set overrides (cli/run.py:471-488, run_config.py:48-56; the config path is explicit, not discovered by a walk), or from Python API arguments. (4) job ids used with squeue/scancel are sbatch stdout tokens passed as list argv (slurm.py:284,375,510-511; scheduler.py:451-452). The local path used by this repository's glue (run_shinkaevolve.py:56, LocalJobConfig without conda_env/activate_script) never reaches slurm.py: local.submit runs a list argv with no shell (local.py:105-113); the activate_script variant uses shlex.join for the python command (scheduler.py:200). The .hydra/config.yaml directory walk (utils_hydra.py:16-32) feeds eval_hydra only, not job command construction (peer-owned resume/deserialization unit). Same-principal quoting gaps recorded under hardening.

checks.invariant: The `shell=True` / create_subprocess_shell invocation in headless.py cannot receive shell syntax from the model string, the prompt, the work dir or the SHINKA_HEADLESS_COMMAND prefix, and no LLM-derived text is placed on the command line.
checks.result: Holds; refuted as a finding. The shell string is always shlex.join(command) executed by /bin/sh (headless.py:212-219, 247-252), so every token is POSIX-quoted. Token origins: prefix = shlex.split(os.getenv('SHINKA_HEADLESS_COMMAND', default)) (headless.py:39-43) - process environment, i.e. the operator's shell or the cwd/package .env loaded with override=True (env.py:17-26); it selects the executable by design but cannot add shell syntax after re-quoting. agent / agent_model / effort come from parse_headless_model (headless.py:64-95) applied to the configured llm_models entry (operator config); the shell path is taken only when agent == 'claude' (headless.py:180-181) and effort is allowlisted (headless.py:85). --prompt-file is <work_dir>/headless_prompts/prompt_<uuid4>.md and --work-dir is the results dir (headless.py:144-147, 161; async_runner.py:209-213). LLM/program-derived text is written only into the prompt file body (headless.py:148-151), never into argv. check_headless_available uses list argv (headless.py:99-107; called from model_availability.py:185). The claude agent is started with `--allow read-only` (headless.py:169-170).

checks.invariant: The remaining process-spawn sites of the three baseline packages build list argv without a shell, and no LLM-controlled value can become an option or an executable name.
checks.result: Holds; refuted as a finding. claude_code.py:67-80,118-125: list argv ['claude','-p','--model',cfg.name,...,'--system-prompt',system_message,'--max-budget-usd',str(budget)]; the user prompt goes through stdin; model/cwd/budget come from the model config, kwargs are not supplied by callers (process_parallel.py:209-212 passes only system_message/messages). copilot_cli.py:118-147,151-157: list argv; the prompt is the value of '-p' (single argv element, no shell), effort allowlisted (copilot_cli.py:133), '--allow-all-tools' only when the operator's config sets allow_all_tools. codex_app_server.py:269-270,352-359: argv is [cfg.codex_bin,'app-server']; the prompt travels as JSON-RPC over stdin with approvalPolicy 'never' and a read-only sandbox (codex_app_server.py:284-288). Provider selection is config-only (ensemble.py:43-47). CodeEvolve evaluator.py:298-305 spawns [sys.executable, eval_path, tmp code file, tmp results file] as list argv. ShinkaEvolve validators (async_apply.py:150-244) pass the fixed gen_N/main.<ext> path as one argv element; the Wolfram check embeds that path through escape_wolfram_string and, on WSL only, shlex.quote (wolfram.py:83-100).

checks.invariant: Unquoted expansions, the echo-built run.json and the pkill pattern in the glue scripts are fed only by the operator's own positional arguments/environment, and no lower-trust reader or writer is involved.
checks.result: Holds; refuted as a finding. framework, problem, model, budget and seed are the five positional arguments of run_baseline.sh (line 17); out is derived from them plus `date` (line 18). No other script in the repository invokes run_baseline.sh or the run_*.py drivers (repository-wide grep: only README.md:53 and the scripts' own usage comments), so no file-, results- or LLM-derived value reaches these expansions. run.json and end.json (lines 56, 64) are written but read by no code in the repository. `pkill -P $$` (line 39) matches by parent pid only and takes no pattern from input. The Python drivers use argparse values in list argv / execv (run_openevolve.py:49-52, run_codeevolve.py:67-69) and yaml.safe_load/safe_dump. setup_baselines.sh interpolates only ${PYTHON313} from the operator environment (line 25). All are same-principal; quoting and arithmetic-expansion notes are under hardening.

checks.invariant: A network client that can reach the vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint started by run_baseline.sh cannot influence the programs the framework generates and executes.
checks.result: No complete source trace; recorded as hardening, not a candidate. run_baseline.sh:34 runs `vllm serve "$@" --port $port` and the callers at lines 47 and 50-51 pass only the model, --runner, --max-model-len, --gpu-memory-utilization, --enable-prefix-caching and --reasoning-parser: no --host and no --api-key, and the clients use the placeholder key 'EMPTY' (run_baseline.sh:22, run_openevolve.py:37, run_codeevolve.py:60, run_shinkaevolve.py:52). The bind interface is therefore whatever vLLM uses when --host is omitted; vLLM is not vendored and its version is not pinned in the repository (setup_baselines.sh:17 takes it from the main environment), so the bind address is a deployment/dependency fact that source cannot settle. Independently of that fact, the step from 'unauthenticated client of the API' to 'controls generated programs' is not present in source: an OpenAI-compatible client receives only responses to its own requests, and the flags passed enable no state-changing server feature (no LoRA runtime loading, no tool parser, no dev-mode endpoints). What a reachable client could do is consume GPU time during a wall-clock-budgeted run and read /v1/models and /metrics. The exact missing fact for any stronger claim is a vLLM server capability, in the deployed version and with these flags, by which one API client alters completions returned to another. The separate case of a listener impersonating the endpoint on the loopback port is the candidate below.

checks.invariant: The process whose completions become executed programs is the vLLM server that run_baseline.sh itself started; another local principal cannot stand in for it on `localhost:<port>`.
checks.result: Not enforced in source; candidate baselines-glue/vllm-localhost-endpoint-impersonation. The port is obtained by bind-and-release (run_baseline.sh:29,42), vLLM is started in the background on it (line 34), and the readiness loop returns success as soon as anything answers `curl -s localhost:$port/v1/models` - the probe runs before the `kill -0 $server` liveness test, has no -f, and never checks that the responder is the started child (line 36). The frameworks then send every prompt to http://localhost:<port>/v1 with the key 'EMPTY' and execute the returned code through the shared evaluation under the operator's uid and environment (run_openevolve.py:37; process_parallel.py:209,283,364; evaluator.py:260,455; openevolve_evaluator.py:11; benchmarks/evaluation.py:43-46; run_evaluator.py:12). Whether a second local principal exists on the host and can take the port (before vLLM listens, or on the IPv6 loopback that an IPv4-only bind leaves free) is not source-visible; see the candidate's blockers.

candidates.title: run_baseline.sh accepts any listener on localhost:<port> as the model server, so another local user can supply the programs the operator executes
candidates.description:
Lower-trust principal: a second unprivileged local user (or other workload sharing the host network namespace) on the GPU host where the operator runs baselines/run_baseline.sh. Accepted input: HTTP responses from whichever process is listening on `localhost:<port>`. Control that should stop it: the launcher should only hand the frameworks an endpoint that is provably the vLLM child it started (and the frameworks should authenticate that endpoint); the only visible checks are a `curl -s localhost:$port/v1/models` probe and a `kill -0 $server` liveness test that is evaluated after the probe has already returned success. Boundary crossed: local user A to code execution as operator B. Affected resource: the operator's account (files, environment variables including any provider keys, EVAL_LOG score integrity), because every completion returned by the endpoint is turned into a program and executed by benchmarks/evaluation.py with the operator's environment.

Source-visible mechanics: (1) free_port binds ('', 0), prints the number and releases the socket; the number is reused later for `vllm serve ... --port $port`, where it is visible in the process arguments. For shinkaevolve the main port is chosen before the embedding server is started and only used after that server is up. (2) `serve` backgrounds vLLM and loops: `curl -s localhost:$port/v1/models > /dev/null && return 0; kill -0 $server || break`. Any HTTP responder satisfies the probe (no -f, no identity check), and success is returned without consulting the child's state, so a vLLM child that failed to bind because the port was taken goes unnoticed. (3) All three drivers configure the framework with `http://localhost:<port>/v1` and the placeholder key 'EMPTY'; vLLM is started without --host and without --api-key, so neither side authenticates the other and the hostname is resolved by each client. (4) The completion text becomes child_code and is executed by the shared evaluation as a subprocess that inherits the operator environment.

Two ways a foreign listener can end up answering, both needing local validation: (a) binding 127.0.0.1:<port> between the `vllm serve` exec (port visible in process arguments) and vLLM's own listen; (b) binding [::1]:<port> at any time if vLLM's default bind covers IPv4 only, with clients that resolve `localhost` to ::1 first. This is not the documented 'generated code runs unsandboxed' trade-off: the party choosing the code is a different local principal than the operator and the operator's own model.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: baselines/run_baseline.sh treats 'something answers HTTP on localhost:<port>' as proof that its own vLLM child is serving: the port is picked by bind-and-release, the readiness probe is evaluated before (and independently of) the child liveness test, and the server/clients share no secret and use the ambiguous hostname `localhost`, so the identity of the endpoint whose output is executed is never established.

trace.description: Readiness loop: `curl -s localhost:$port/v1/models > /dev/null && return 0` succeeds for any HTTP responder on that port and returns before `kill -0 $server` is consulted; a foreign listener's response is accepted here as 'vLLM is up'.
The same port is handed to the framework driver (`--port $port`); lines 59 and 60 do the same for shinkaevolve (plus --embed-port) and codeevolve.
OpenEvolve is configured with api_base `http://localhost:{port}/v1` and api_key 'EMPTY'; no credential or identity ties the client to the vLLM child.
AsyncOpenAI client is created with base_url=self.api_base; all completions are requested from whichever process holds that address.
llm_response is obtained from the endpoint via _worker_llm_ensemble.generate_with_context.
Diff blocks extracted from the response are applied to the parent program to form child_code (full-rewrite mode takes the response's code block instead).
The code is written to a temp file (line 260) and the configured evaluate function is called with its path.
The glue evaluator forwards the program path to the shared benchmarks evaluation.
subprocess.Popen runs run_evaluator.py on the program with env={**os.environ, ...} (line 46): the operator's uid and full environment, no isolation beyond a temp cwd and a 60 s limit.
module.evaluate(program_path) runs the problem evaluator, which imports/executes the program text supplied by the endpoint.

evidence.description: free_port: `s.bind(('', 0)); print(s.getsockname()[1])` - the socket is released when the helper exits, so the returned port is unreserved until vLLM binds it.
`vllm serve "$@" --port $port >> $log 2>&1 &` - started in the background with the port in its arguments, without --host and without --api-key; a bind failure is only written to the log.
Strongest visible control: probe then liveness. The probe has no -f and no responder identity check, and `return 0` short-circuits before `kill -0 $server`.
`port=$(free_port)` is taken before the optional embedding server is started and awaited (lines 46-47) and is only bound at line 50.
`OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY` is exported: the clients present a placeholder, so no shared secret exists between launcher, server and frameworks.
ShinkaEvolve path of the same root cause: every LLM role uses `local/{model}@http://localhost:{port}/v1` (embedding endpoint at line 45).
CodeEvolve path of the same root cause: API_BASE=`http://localhost:{port}/v1`, API_KEY='EMPTY'.
The evaluated program inherits the operator's whole environment (`env={**os.environ, **SINGLE_THREAD}`).

blockers: No target code may be executed in this run (sandbox controls incomplete), so the readiness-gate behaviour of `serve` with a foreign listener and a failed/absent vLLM child has not been observed.

Deployment fact: whether the benchmark host has a second local principal (other user accounts, or unprivileged workloads sharing the host network namespace) that can read process arguments (/proc not mounted with hidepid) or probe loopback ports during a run.

Dependency fact (vLLM is not vendored and its version is not pinned in the repository): how long `vllm serve` takes from exec to listen() on --port, and which address family/interface it binds when --host is omitted (IPv4 wildcard only versus dual-stack); this decides whether 127.0.0.1:<port> can be taken first or [::1]:<port> stays free for the whole run.
Host fact: the order in which `localhost` resolves (::1 versus 127.0.0.1) for curl and for the OpenAI/httpx clients used by the three frameworks.

validation_plan.local: In the no-network sandbox with isolated loopback and dummy data only. Step 1 (readiness gate): create scratch/bin/vllm as a stub script that sleeps 3 seconds and exits 1 (stand-in for a vLLM child that could not bind) and put scratch/bin first on PATH. Start a dummy HTTP listener (python3 http.server subclass) on 127.0.0.1:P, P a free port, that answers every GET with the body {"sentinel":"foreign-listener"}. Copy lines 29-38 of baselines/run_baseline.sh (free_port and serve) verbatim into scratch/harness.sh and append: `serve P scratch/vllm.log dummy-model; echo "serve_rc=$?" > scratch/poc_marker`. Run it under `bash` with `set -u`, 30 s wall-clock limit. Observable that proves the boundary result: scratch/poc_marker contains `serve_rc=0` and stdout does not contain 'vLLM did not start', although the stub child exited 1 and never listened. Step 2 (address-family split): bind a dummy listener on 0.0.0.0:P2 answering {"sentinel":"own-server"} (stand-in for an IPv4-wildcard bind), then try to bind a second listener on [::1]:P2 answering {"sentinel":"foreign-listener"}; write to scratch/poc_family whether the second bind succeeded and which sentinel is returned by `curl -s localhost:P2/v1/models` and by Python `urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:P2/v1/models')`. Stop all listeners afterwards. Nothing beyond these marker files is produced.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on the benchmark host during one run: record the listening address of the vLLM process for the run's port (`ss -ltnp`), the output of `getent ahosts localhost`, whether other user accounts or shared-network containers exist on the host, whether /proc is mounted with hidepid, and whether a host firewall filters the port from other machines.

hardening: baselines/run_baseline.sh:34,47,50 - `vllm serve` is started without --host and without --api-key, and the clients use the key 'EMPTY'. Whether the port is reachable from other machines depends on vLLM's default bind when --host is omitted (not source-visible; vLLM is unpinned and unvendored). No source path lets a remote API client alter completions served to the framework, so this is exposure of GPU capacity and of /v1/models and /metrics, not a candidate. Pass `--host 127.0.0.1` and a per-run random `--api-key`, hand that key to the three drivers instead of 'EMPTY', and use 127.0.0.1 instead of `localhost` in run_openevolve.py:37, run_shinkaevolve.py:33,45 and run_codeevolve.py:60.

baselines/run_baseline.sh:36 - make the readiness check fail closed: test `kill -0 $server` before accepting the probe, use `curl -sf`, and after the loop confirm the child is still alive (or have vLLM listen on a unix socket / a pre-bound inherited socket instead of a released port from free_port at line 29).

baselines/run_baseline.sh:17-19,26,43,50,55-60 - positional arguments are expanded unquoted (`mkdir -p $out`, `basename $model`, `[ $framework = ... ]`, `--problem $problem --model $model --output $out`) and `$((budget * 60))` performs bash arithmetic evaluation on a raw argument. Only the operator supplies these values (same principal), so this is robustness: quote every expansion, validate framework against the three names, require problem to match a directory name under benchmarks/problems, and require budget/seed to match ^[0-9]+$.

baselines/run_baseline.sh:56,64 - run.json/end.json are assembled with echo and raw interpolation of problem, model, budget, seed and the nvidia-smi GPU name; a quote or backslash in any of them yields invalid or restructured JSON. No code in the repository reads these files today; write them with `python -c 'json.dump(...)'` so later analysis tooling can rely on them.

baselines/ShinkaEvolve/shinka/launch/slurm.py:20,27,133-134,155,183,228-250,259,271,329,340,352,441-447,475,481,489 - env exports, `" ".join(cmd)`, log_dir, image, docker_flags, image_tar_path, modules and sbatch kwargs are formatted into shell text without shlex.quote. All values are operator job/evolution config (same principal; results_dir with a space or metacharacter breaks the job or self-injects). Use shlex.join(cmd) and shlex.quote for each interpolated value, as scheduler.py:200 already does for the local activate_script path.

baselines/ShinkaEvolve/shinka/launch/slurm.py:49-50,64-68 and scheduler.py:196-200 - _escape_double_quotes only escapes `"`; inside the resulting double-quoted `source "..."` string `$(...)`, backticks and `\` are still interpreted. Operator-controlled today; prefer shlex.quote. Also slurm.py:259 and 340 append `#SBATCH --k=v` entries without a newline, so more than one extra sbatch kwarg produces a single malformed directive (correctness).

baselines/ShinkaEvolve/shinka/llm/providers/headless.py:212-219,247-252 - `shell=True` / create_subprocess_shell is used only for the claude agent and only with shlex.join output; it adds nothing over list argv and should be dropped so a future edit cannot introduce an unquoted token.

baselines/ShinkaEvolve/shinka/env.py:17-26 - `<cwd>/.env` and `<package root>/.env` are loaded with override=True at `import shinka`. They can replace PATH, PYTHONPATH, SHINKA_HEADLESS_COMMAND (headless.py:40) and WOLFRAMSCRIPT_BIN (utils/wolfram.py:20), which select the executables that later subprocess calls run. Consider override=False and an allowlist of keys (provider API keys) for the cwd file. See the `uncovered` entry.

baselines/openevolve/openevolve/llm/copilot_cli.py:118-121 - the whole prompt (system message plus prior programs and program output) is passed as one argv element: it is visible to other local users in the process list and is subject to the per-argument size limit that claude_code.py:82-83 already avoids by using stdin.

baselines/openevolve/openevolve/llm/claude_code.py:67-80,118-125 - `claude -p` is launched with no tool/permission restriction flags and with cwd defaulting to the framework's working directory, while the prompt contains program output fed back from evaluations; ShinkaEvolve's headless path passes `--allow read-only` (headless.py:169-170) and the codex backend sets a read-only sandbox (codex_app_server.py:286-287). Not used by this repository's glue (which uses the OpenAI-compatible provider); align the claude and copilot backends with an explicit read-only/no-tools setting and a dedicated empty cwd.

uncovered.surface: ShinkaEvolve dotenv auto-loading at import: `<cwd>/.env` and `<package root>/.env` loaded with override=True (shinka/env.py), re-invoked from shinka/__init__.py, llm/client.py, llm/constants.py, embed/client.py, cli/models.py and launch_hydra.py
uncovered.boundary: Author of on-disk state in the directory a shinka CLI is started from (a downloaded task or results directory) vs. the process environment that selects executables and endpoints (PATH, PYTHONPATH, SHINKA_HEADLESS_COMMAND, WOLFRAMSCRIPT_BIN, provider API base/keys)
uncovered.subsystem: baselines/ShinkaEvolve (shinka package import, CLIs shinka_run / shinka_launch / shinka_visualize)
uncovered.reason: Found while tracing the origin of the SHINKA_HEADLESS_COMMAND prefix. It is a different boundary from command-string construction (environment override from a data directory, not shell quoting) and needs its own unit to decide whether a data-only workflow such as `shinka_visualize` run inside a received results directory lets that directory's .env choose executables later resolved through PATH (python/git/pandoc/wkhtmltopdf/npx) or redirect provider endpoints and keys. Not assessed here beyond confirming the load order and override=True; within this repository's glue the cwd is the operator's own repository root (run_baseline.sh:15).
